candidates.attacker_control: The archive bytes, specifically ZipEntry names. java.util.zip.ZipFile (used at ZipUtil.java:383) returns entry names verbatim and does not reject `../`; the library performs no sanitization. Any caller that extracts an attacker-supplied ZIP via ZipUtil.unzip(...) (e.g. unzip(String zipFilePath, String outFileDir) at lines 338-353) hands the entry name directly to File construction.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Confirmed there is no normalization/canonical-path check in the unzip family (lines 280-472) or in FileUtil.file/touch/mkParentDirs/getOutputStream; `getCanonicalPath`/containment logic exists only in ZipUtil.validateFiles for compression (771). zipEntry.isDirectory() only selects mkdirs vs write, and unzipFileBytes reads into memory without writing. JDK ZipFile is the entry source and does not sanitize names. XmlUtil was separately checked and does disable XXE (XmlUtil.java:791-819), so this is not an XXE snapshot.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite outside the extraction directory with attacker-controlled content, limited only by process permissions. Typical consequences are overwriting configuration, script/cron/startup files, deployed classes/JSPs, or other writable application files, which can lead to code execution, data tampering, or denial of service (e.g., clobbering critical files). Read access to arbitrary files is not provided by this specific path.
candidates.prerequisites: An application uses Hutool's ZipUtil.unzip/unzip-with-directory API to extract an archive whose contents are attacker-influenced (uploaded archive, downloaded plugin/theme, imported backup, etc.). The process must have write permission to the traversal target. No special configuration or opt-in is needed; the vulnerable path is the default public API.
candidates.root_cause: ZipUtil.unzip(File, File, Charset) iterates the archive entries and builds the destination as `outItemFile = new File(outFile, zipEntry.getName())` (line 389) without normalizing/canonicalizing the resulting path or verifying it stays under `outFile`. FileUtil.file(File,String) is just `new File(parent, path)` (FileUtil.java:336-340), and the subsequent FileUtil.touch(outItemFile) (line 393) plus copy() (line 394 -> 805-816 -> FileUtil.getOutputStream, which calls touch -> mkParentDirs/mkdirs at FileUtil.java:604-617, 651-657, 2390-2396) silently create missing parent directories and open/write the target. Entry names containing `../` (or `..\` on Windows) therefore escape the intended output directory. The same class validates containment for the reverse operation (validateFiles, ZipUtil.java:763-782), but no equivalent check exists in the unzip path; no `slipCheck`/canonical-path guard is present anywhere.
candidates.title: Zip Slip path traversal in ZipUtil.unzip lets a crafted ZIP write files outside the extraction directory
candidates.trace: unzip(String zipFilePath, String outFileDir[, Charset]) (ZipUtil.java:338-353) -> unzip(File zipFile, File outFile, Charset) (378-403): new ZipFile(...) (383) -> enumerate entries (384-388) -> new File(outFile, zipEntry.getName()) (389) -> FileUtil.touch(outItemFile) creates missing parents and the file (393; FileUtil.java:604-617, 651-657) -> copy(zipFileObj, zipEntry, outItemFile) (394) -> FileUtil.getOutputStream(outItemFile) -> new FileOutputStream (805-816; FileUtil.java:2390-2396) writes attacker-controlled bytes to the traversed path. Directory entries also take the mkdirs() branch (390-391).
candidates.unverified: No execution, archive crafting, or runtime testing was performed (read-only review). Exact writable paths and exploitability depend on the consuming application's call site, working directory, and OS permissions; Windows backslash handling was reasoned from Java File semantics, not tested.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') / Zip Slip

coverage_summary: Reviewed the 790-file source scope (all Java main sources under hutool-core, hutool-http, hutool-extra, hutool-json, hutool-db, hutool-crypto, hutool-captcha, hutool-cron, hutool-setting, hutool-poi, hutool-script, hutool-log, hutool-system, hutool-aop, hutool-bloomFilter, plus docs/bin assets). Focused deep reads on the extraction/IO path (ZipUtil, FileUtil), XML parsing (XmlUtil), HTTP/TLS (HttpConnection, SSLSocketFactoryBuilder, DefaultTrustManager, TrustAnyHostnameVerifier), multipart upload handling (MultipartFormData/UploadFile/UploadFileHeader), randomness (RandomUtil, captcha), and deserialization helpers (ObjectUtil/IoUtil/XmlUtil); grepped for Runtime.exec, ObjectInputStream, XMLDecoder, DocumentBuilderFactory/SAXParserFactory, Class.forName, zip-extraction sinks, canonical-path checks, and weak RNG usage. Non-Java documentation/JS/CSS assets were not security-reviewed.
limitations: Read-only static review: no code executed, no archives built/extracted, no runtime confirmation of exploitability.
No test sources exist in the snapshot (only src/main), and no version history/patch information is available, so the finding is based solely on this source state.
Not every one of the 790 files was read line-by-line; coverage prioritized input-handling and security-relevant modules, so additional low-signal issues may exist in unread utility code.
Real-world impact of the Zip Slip depends on the consuming application's call site and file permissions, which are outside this repository.
No external CVE/ground-truth data was consulted (per review rules); the version/CVE association is contextual, not verified against an advisory database.

rejected_leads.lead: hutool-http disables HTTPS server validation by default: HttpConnection.openHttp uses TrustAnyHostnameVerifier when none is set (HttpConnection.java:578) and SSLSocketFactoryBuilder defaults to DefaultTrustManager, whose checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted are empty (SSLSocketFactoryBuilder.java:40, DefaultTrustManager.java:20-26).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine default-insecure TLS behavior with MITM impact, but it is explicitly documented as intended in HttpRequest.setHostnameVerifier ('如果不设置，不做验证，所有域名被信任', HttpRequest.java:717-719) and requires a network adversary; it is not the version-specific defect in this snapshot, so the ZIP extraction path traversal was chosen as stronger/cleaner evidenced.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe deserialization helper APIs: XmlUtil.readObjectFromXml uses java.beans.XMLDecoder (XmlUtil.java:198-208), ObjectUtil.unserialize uses ObjectInputStream (ObjectUtil.java:322-331), and IoUtil.readObj (IoUtil.java:550-560).
rejected_leads.reason: These are explicit, documented deserialization entry points that only become exploitable if a caller feeds them untrusted data; the code does no validation, but the APIs' purpose is to deserialize objects, so this is a caller-responsibility design hazard rather than a clear library defect in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: RandomUtil.randomString uses ThreadLocalRandom (RandomUtil.java:370-382) and is used to generate captcha codes (RandomGenerator.java:40-42), i.e. a non-cryptographic RNG for security-adjacent values.
rejected_leads.reason: CWE-338 weakness is real but no concrete predictability/exploit path could be established from source alone; ThreadLocalRandom state is not externally observable, so impact is unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: SqlBuilder.in concatenates caller values directly into SQL text (SqlBuilder.java:328-331); identifiers/table names are also concatenated throughout SqlBuilder.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an application to pass untrusted values to this fluent builder; other value paths use '?' placeholders (e.g. insert/update at lines 142, 200), and identifier concatenation is the documented API contract, so this is an unconfirmed injection lead rather than the repository's strongest evidenced issue.

summary: Static review of the Hutool 4.1.11 snapshot (790 files; Java library modules plus docs/bin assets). The strongest, best-evidenced issue is a Zip Slip (CWE-22) in cn.hutool.core.util.ZipUtil.unzip: archive entry names are turned directly into output File objects with no containment/canonical-path check, and the write helpers create parent directories and overwrite/create the target, so a crafted ZIP whose entries contain "../" writes attacker-controlled content anywhere the process can write. This matches the known vulnerable version (Hutool 4.1.11) and the class already performs a containment check for the opposite direction (zip creation), showing the missing validation in extraction. XXE was checked and is mitigated in XmlUtil (disableXXE). Other plausible leads (default trust-all HTTPS in hutool-http, XMLDecoder/Java deserialization helper APIs, non-CSPRNG RandomUtil, raw-value SqlBuilder.in) are recorded as rejected/unconfirmed rather than submitted.
